summary: The root فَأَد (faʾada) primarily refers to the heart, specifically the organ itself. It can also denote the intellect or understanding, as the heart was considered the seat of these faculties.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: (T, S, M, A, L, K,) aor. فَأََ, inf. n. فَأْدٌ, (M, L,) He, or it, hit, struck, smote, affected, or hurt, his (a man's, K) فُؤَاد [or heart, &c.]: (S, M, L, K:) he hit, or smote, him, (AZ, T,) or shot, or shot at, and hit, or smote, him, namely a gazelle, (A,) or an animal of the chase, (AZ, T,) in his فُؤَاد. (AZ, T, A.) And, said of a disease, (S,) and of fear, (A,) It smote, or affected, his فُؤَاد: (S, A:) or, said of fear, it rendered him cowardly.

i. q. تَوَقَّدَ [i. e., when said of fuel, It burned, burned up, burned brightly or fiercely, blazed, or flamed ]: (M, L, K:) [and] so when said of the heart [i. e. It became excited with ardour, or eagerness ]. (M, L, K. *) And i. q. تَحَرَّقَ [ It burned much, as a quasi-pass. v.]: (so in copies of the K, in SM's copy and in my MS.
They lighted a fire (M, A, L, K) for the purpose of roasting. (A) See also 1, latter half.
: [see 1, of which it is the inf. n.: and] see the paragraph here following.

(S, M, A, Msb, K, &c.) and فَوَادٌ, which is strange, (K,) but said by Esh-Shiháb to be a dial var., and to be without reason disallowed by AHát; (TA;) of the masc. gender only; (Lh, M, L, K, &c.;) The heart; syn. قَلْبٌ [q. v.]; (S, M, A, L, Msb, K, &c.;) of man, and of an animal other than man: (M, L:) so called because of its تَفَأُّد (T, M, L, K) i. e.

: see مَفْؤُودٌ, in two places. Also, (T, M, L,) applied to bread [or dough], (M, L,) and so, (M, L, K,) and, and, (K,) Baked on the fire: (T:) or put into hot ashes, (L, K,) and baked therein: (L:) or toasted [or baked ] in hot ashes. (M, L.) And the first, (T, S, M, &c.,) applied to flesh-meat, (S, M, L,) Roasted, (T, S, M, L, K,) as also, (M, L, K,) on the fire: (T:) or roasted upon live coals; as also [evidently, I think, a mistranscription for ].

A place which one makes, for a cake of bread, or lump of dough, in hot ashes, or in a fire, to put it therein [ for the purpose of baking it ]: (S, M, * L, K: *) pl. أَفَائِيدُ. (L.) See also فَئِيدٌ.

(T, S, M, L, K) and (S, L, K) and (T, M, L, K) The [ iron instrument, with which flesh-meat is roasted, called ] سَفُّود, (T, S, M, L, K,) [or] with which one roasts and bakes. (L, TA.) And [in the CK “ or ”] the first, (S, L, K,) and the second and third also, (accord. to the K,) the piece of wood, or wooden implement, with which the [ fire in the kind of oven called ] تَنُّور is stirred: pl. مَفَائِدُ. (S, L, K.)

Hit, struck, smitten, affected, or hurt, in his فُؤَاد [or heart, &c.]: (S, A, L:) smitten, or affected, by a disease therein: (S, L:) or by pain therein. (L.) A man without a heart; having no heart; as also: (Ks, S, L:) weak-hearted: (T, L:) a coward; (T, M, L, K;) and so: (T, K:) in this sense it has no verb. (AAF, IJ, M, L.) See also فَئِيدٌ, in two places.
: see فَئِيدٌ, in two places. Also A place of fuel: (T, L:) a place in which a fire is lighted for roasting. (A.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
